acceptance_criteria.criterion: A valid .tar.xz archive extracts all entries into the target directory.
A tar entry resolving outside the target throws InvalidDataException.
CompositeArchiveExtractor dispatches to ZipArchiveExtractor for "zip" and TarXzArchiveExtractor for "tar.xz", and throws NotSupportedException for unknown types.
SharpCompress is the only new package reference added in this WP.

summary: Implemented TarXzArchiveExtractor using SharpCompress XZStream for decompression and System.Formats.Tar.TarReader for tar parsing. Includes Tar-Slip protection rejecting any entry resolving outside the destination directory.

Implemented CompositeArchiveExtractor with constructor injection of IArchiveExtractor dependencies; dispatches by file extension ('zip' to ZipArchiveExtractor, 'tar.xz' to TarXzArchiveExtractor, unknown throws NotSupportedException). Provides a parameterless default constructor wiring concrete implementations.
Added SharpCompress 0.38.0 package reference to VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.csproj (sole new dependency for this WP).

Created TarXzArchiveExtractorTests.cs with 8 tests (7 pass, 1 SkippableFact skipped): flat extraction, nested-directory preservation, Tar-Slip exception, Tar-Slip no-files-outside-dest, composite .zip dispatch, composite .tar.xz dispatch, composite unknown extension NotSupportedException. Pre-built .tar.xz fixtures embedded as byte arrays generated via Python. All 62 infrastructure tests pass, 0 regressions.

comments.note: The separator normalisation (replacing '/' with Path.DirectorySeparatorChar) handles Unix-origin tar entries on Windows correctly; however it also means that entry names containing backslashes on non-Windows hosts are treated as path separators. This is the same trade-off made by ZipArchiveExtractor and is consistent within this codebase, but worth documenting if cross-platform archive compatibility becomes a concern.

The parameterless constructor wires concrete classes directly, making it useful for DI registrations that call new() but bypassing the container. A future refactor to use a factory pattern or DI registration helper would remove this hidden coupling — low priority now but worth noting when WP-007 registers these types in the DI container.

Test fixture archives are embedded as hardcoded byte arrays generated by a one-off Python script. SharpCompress TarWriter does not expose an XZ write path, making programmatic generation impractical from C#. The byte arrays should be stored as binary test assets (e.g., in a Fixtures/archives/ folder) rather than inline literals to improve readability and allow future re-generation.

comments.note: Symlink tar entries (TarEntryType.SymbolicLink, HardLink) are not filtered before calling ExtractToFileAsync. The Tar-Slip guard checks the entry name (the symlink file path inside the archive), but does not inspect the symlink target. A malicious archive could create a symlink inside the destination that points to a path outside it, bypassing the guard. Recommend filtering or explicitly skipping SymbolicLink and HardLink entries in TarXzArchiveExtractor.ExtractAsync.

ExtractAsync_TraversalEntry_LeavesNoFilesOutsideDestination uses Slip2TarXzBytes (safe.txt first, then ../evil.txt). The test verifies evil.txt is absent outside dest but does not assert whether safe.txt was written before the throw. This is fine for the AC, but a complementary assertion (e.g. Assert.False(File.Exists(safe_path)) or Assert.True) would document the expected partial-write behavior explicitly.

No observations beyond those already noted by the Developer — code is clean, Tar-Slip guard is correct for file entries, separator normalisation is consistent with ZipArchiveExtractor, and CancellationToken propagation is correct throughout the extraction loop.

summary: Reviewed 4 files (TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs, CompositeArchiveExtractor.cs, VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.csproj, TarXzArchiveExtractorTests.cs). 0 Critical, 1 High (SymbolicLink/HardLink Tar-Slip bypass), 1 Medium (no audit logging), 0 Low. FAIL — routes to Developer for remediation of the High finding before re-audit.

comments.note: [HIGH] A01 Broken Access Control / A03 Injection — Symlink/HardLink Tar-Slip bypass. File: src/VideoIndexer.Infrastructure/ExternalTools/TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs, lines 53-57 (entry-type filter) and line 74 (ExtractToFileAsync). The entry-type skip block excludes Directory and GlobalExtendedAttributes but does NOT exclude SymbolicLink or HardLink. The Tar-Slip guard (lines 62-66) validates entry.Name — the path inside the archive where the link will be created — but never inspects entry.LinkName (the symlink target). A crafted archive can include an entry with entry.Name='link' (inside dest, passes the guard) and entry.LinkName='../../../../etc/cron.d/backdoor' (absolute or relative path escaping dest). System.Formats.Tar TarReader.ExtractToFileAsync faithfully creates that symlink on disk; any subsequent read/write that follows it escapes the destination. On Windows, HardLink entries create a hard link to an arbitrary existing file, bypassing the name guard entirely. Remediation: Add a guard immediately before the name-normalisation block to throw InvalidDataException for SymbolicLink and HardLink entries, consistent with how traversal entries are already rejected: if (entry.EntryType is TarEntryType.SymbolicLink or TarEntryType.HardLink) { throw new InvalidDataException($"Archive entry '{entry.Name}' is a symbolic or hard link and was rejected."); } Also add a corresponding test — e.g. a fixture archive containing a symlink entry — so the guard is covered by the test suite.

[MEDIUM] A09 Security Logging & Monitoring Failures — TarXzArchiveExtractor performs no audit logging. Extracting externally-downloaded binaries (ffmpeg) is a security-sensitive filesystem operation; neither successful extraction nor guard-triggered rejections produce any log output. If the provisioning pipeline is ever fed a tampered archive, there is no audit trail. Recommendation: inject or reference ILogger<TarXzArchiveExtractor> (consistent with the rest of the infrastructure layer) and emit at least: (a) one Debug entry when extraction begins (archivePath, destinationDirectory), (b) one Warning entry for each rejected entry, and (c) one Information entry on completion (entry count). This does not block the current FAIL — address after the High finding is resolved.

summary: REWORK: Fixed HIGH security finding — added SymbolicLink/HardLink guard in TarXzArchiveExtractor.ExtractAsync that throws InvalidDataException for those entry types unconditionally. A symlink whose Name is within the destination but whose LinkName points outside it would have bypassed the Tar-Slip guard.
Added regression test ExtractAsync_SymlinkEntry_ThrowsInvalidDataException using a pre-built fixture with a symlink entry whose target resolves far outside the destination directory.
All 63 infrastructure tests pass (1 SkippableFact skipped — fixture file absent as expected). 0 regressions.

comments.note: Symlink/HardLink guard added immediately after the directory-skip block. This is the minimal, correct fix: we reject the entire entry type rather than attempt to validate the LinkName path, because LinkName values can be relative or absolute and require OS-level symlink resolution to evaluate accurately. Rejection is the only safe option.

comments.note: The symlink guard is unconditional rejection rather than LinkName path validation. This is the correct and only safe approach: LinkName values can be relative or absolute, may require OS-level symlink resolution to evaluate, and the specification provides no use-case requiring symlinks in the ffmpeg archive. Consistent with the existing Tar-Slip guard philosophy of reject-on-suspicion.

No regressions found in VideoIndexer.Tests (42 tests) or VideoIndexer.App.Tests (39 tests). Guard placement (before name normalisation) is correct and does not interfere with any other extraction path.

summary: Re-audit of rework changes in TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs (lines 64-69) and new symlink fixture test. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (logging gap carried over — not in scope for this WP), 1 Low (overwrite: true), 1 Info (unfiltered special device entry types). HIGH finding from first audit is fully remediated. Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: HIGH FINDING RESOLVED. The SymbolicLink/HardLink guard at TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs lines 64-69 correctly throws InvalidDataException unconditionally for TarEntryType.SymbolicLink and TarEntryType.HardLink. The guard is placed BEFORE path normalization and before ExtractToFileAsync — the only safe position, since LinkName values (the symlink target) cannot be reliably validated without OS-level symlink resolution. Rejection is the correct approach and is consistent with the existing Tar-Slip guard philosophy. New test ExtractAsync_SymlinkEntry_ThrowsInvalidDataException uses a fixture with Name='link' (inside dest) and LinkName='../../../../etc/passwd' (outside), which would have bypassed the old name-only guard — it now throws as required.

[MEDIUM — CARRIED OVER] A09 Security Logging & Monitoring Failures — TarXzArchiveExtractor.ExtractAsync emits no log output. Neither successful extraction, rejected symlink entries, nor Tar-Slip guard triggers are logged. The infrastructure layer already has ILogger<T> usage elsewhere; injecting ILogger<TarXzArchiveExtractor> and emitting Debug (start), Warning (rejected entry), and Information (completion with count) would provide an audit trail for security-sensitive filesystem operations. Not blocking this WP — address when logging is added to the provisioning pipeline.

[LOW] A04 Insecure Design — ExtractToFileAsync is called with overwrite: true (TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs line 88). A crafted archive with duplicate entry names could silently overwrite files written earlier in the same extraction pass. Risk is minimal in this use case (the destination directory is freshly created per provisioning run), but for defense-in-depth the extractor could throw on a duplicate entry name rather than silently overwriting.

[INFO] Defense-in-depth — Special device entry types (TarEntryType.BlockDevice, CharacterDevice, Fifo, ContiguousFile) are not explicitly filtered; only SymbolicLink, HardLink, Directory, and GlobalExtendedAttributes are handled. On Windows, ExtractToFileAsync cannot create real device nodes for BlockDevice/CharacterDevice/Fifo, so no immediate exploitation path exists. On Linux hosts, this warrants an explicit reject guard. Low priority given Windows is the primary deployment target and ffmpeg archives do not contain device nodes. Recommended: extend the reject guard to cover BlockDevice, CharacterDevice, and Fifo for cross-platform safety.

[INFO] SharpCompress 0.38.0 dependency audit — no published CVEs identified for this version. The library is used exclusively for XZStream decompression; the file entry extraction path uses the .NET BCL System.Formats.Tar, limiting SharpCompress attack surface to the XZ decompression layer only. No advisory findings.

summary: Code review PASS with one Fix-Forward applied. Architecture is clean, guard ordering is correct (SymbolicLink/HardLink guard before Tar-Slip path guard before ExtractToFileAsync), and all four acceptance criteria are met. Fixed leaveOpen: false → leaveOpen: true on TarReader in TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs: with leaveOpen: false the TarReader.Dispose() call was closing xzStream, then the outer await using xzStream attempted a second dispose — double-dispose of SharpCompress.XZStream. Ownership semantics now correctly reflect that xzStream lifetime is managed by the outer await using scope. All 63 infrastructure tests pass post-fix (1 intentional SkippableFact skip). CompositeArchiveExtractor is idiomatic: null-guards in constructor, switch-expression dispatch, direct Task return avoids unnecessary state machine allocation.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied: changed TarReader constructor argument from leaveOpen: false to leaveOpen: true in TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs. With leaveOpen: false, TarReader.Dispose() disposes xzStream, then the outer await using xzStream disposes it a second time. While many .NET streams handle double-dispose gracefully, SharpCompress.XZStream does not guarantee idempotent disposal and the pattern violates stream ownership conventions. Changed to leaveOpen: true — xzStream is owned by and disposed by the outer await using scope. Non-behavioral change: extraction logic and error paths are identical. 63/63 tests pass post-fix.

[documentation-forward] TarXzArchiveExtractor.ExtractAsync has no ILogger injection. The Security Auditor flagged this as a MEDIUM A09 finding (carried from security-audit pipeline). When logging is added to the provisioning pipeline, this class should inject ILogger<TarXzArchiveExtractor> (consistent with the rest of VideoIndexer.Infrastructure) and emit: Debug on extraction start (archivePath, destinationDirectory), Warning for each rejected entry (symlink/hardlink/traversal), and Information on completion (entry count). Add a documentation note or TODO comment in TarXzArchiveExtractor.cs referencing this gap.

[documentation-forward] TarXzArchiveExtractorTests.cs embeds .tar.xz fixture archives as hardcoded byte[] literals (FlatTarXzBytes, NestedTarXzBytes, SlipTarXzBytes, Slip2TarXzBytes, SymlinkTarXzBytes). The Developer noted these were generated by a one-off Python script because SharpCompress has no XZ write path. Add a comment block in the test file (or a separate fixtures/README.md) documenting: (1) the Python script used to regenerate these arrays, (2) the tar entry structure of each fixture, (3) the instruction to update both the script output and the byte array if fixture content needs to change. This prevents future maintainers from being unable to regenerate the archives.

CompositeArchiveExtractor.ExtractAsync returns Task directly from the switch expression without async/await — correct pattern that avoids allocating a state machine for a pure-dispatch method. No state machine overhead on either the zip or tar.xz path.

Security Auditor INFO: TarEntryType.BlockDevice, CharacterDevice, and Fifo are not explicitly filtered. On Windows (primary target) these cannot be created by ExtractToFileAsync. For cross-platform robustness, a future WP should extend the reject guard to cover these types alongside SymbolicLink and HardLink. Low priority given Windows deployment target and ffmpeg archives do not contain device nodes.
